courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: To log users in,
we got another endpoint
we have to send the request to, it's this endpoint here which you can find in the official docs.
So let's copy that and
let's go to the auth service.
Now I did already add a login method but right now, we're not doing too much here,
we're just setting this userIsAuthenticated here,
I'll get rid of that for now since we'll soon change this anyways.
So in here, I of course still want to send a HTTP request and that still is a post request
as you can see in the official docs and I want to send that request to the URL I just copied where
I also need to inject my API key again, hence I'll use back ticks here so that I can replace this API
key in a very easy way.
So here I'll now add my injected part,
I'll reach out to the environment object and get that Firebase API key.
Now the data we have to pass here is exactly the same data we passed for signing up, it's an e-mail/password
and returnSecureToken,
so let's prepare this object now as a second argument where I forward that e-mail and for that of course,
I expect to get an e-mail here and I get a password here in the login method,
so let's make sure we get these two arguments
and then here I forward the e-mail and I forward the password, like this. Of course I want to return this
so that we can interact with that observable and wait for it to complete
and that takes us back to the auth page then. Here
I do call login and of course that is now not the place where I want to call it anymore,
I want to call it here but only if we are logging in. Now theoretically, we could add an if check or we
will actually add an if check with isLogin and check what our current mode is
and then we send different requests.
Now I don't really want to copy and repeat that entire part here,
we can reuse a lot of that,
instead I only want to basically swap the observable to which we subscribe because the things we then
do with the result are the same. In a success case, we log the user in and then we continue, in an error
case, we show an error message and therefore I will add a new variable here, authObs for auth observable
which will be of type observable which you need to import from rxjs and the type declaration
here is optional but it improves our code quality. Observable is a generic type that holds information
about which data it will eventually yield
and here in our case, that would be that auth response data we get back here,
so we actually can export this interface defined in auth service so that we can import it in this file
and use that auth response data here which you then need to add to your imports from the auth service file.
So now, this is the observable and this will now either hold the observable created for signing up or
for logging in.
So if we have this isLogin, then authObs will be equal to this auth service login where I forward e-mail
and password.
Now important, to avoid errors here with Typescript, in a login case I also now need to use the generic
post method here
so that I define which type of data I get back here which will be auth response data
so that in the auth page, it knows that it is ok to store the result of login here in authObs which expects
an observable that yields auth response data.
So if you add that type annotation, you need to add it everywhere in this chain.
Now in the else case here, so if we're not logging in, then we're signing up, then authObs will be equal to
this auth service sign-up
but without the subscribe call. And now the advantage of this approach is that here after this if check,
I can simply use the authObs and this will now be either the one for logging in or for signing me up
but what I do with the response is then exactly the same. Of course
now I need to add some new checks for error messages,
we could do this with a switch statement too,
I basically only want to check for two extra error messages, e-mail not found and invalid password,
so here I'll add an else/if code equals e-mail not found,
well then my message could be e-mail address could not be found
and else/if the code is equal to invalid password, then I will set the message to this password is not
correct and of course you could be less specific to give the user less hints about why authentication
failed
if you want to do that for security reasons.
So now, we are having the logic in here that should also allow us to sign users in,
let's simply give this a try.
Let's save everything and let's go back to the Ionic app and now, I'll try to login with a user that
actually exists with valid credentials and this looks good.
Now if I first try to sign-up, this fails,
now let's test a different e-mail address, that also exists,
let's test one that does not exist,
e-mail address could not be found,
now let's test a valid e-mail address but an invalid password, password is not correct.
So this all works,
the only thing that is not working as expected is that I'm not getting forwarded
if I do login indeed, though I make it here into that success case because I'm clearly logging my response.
That only happens though because in auth service, I of course
now remove the code where I set this userIsAuthenticated to true and therefore, this never is true
and therefore our guard never allows us access,
so this is actually working as intended and indeed the next task will be to also manage that authentication
state correctly
now.
